name: Neo4j, Inc. (formerly Neo Technology)
origin_detail: Founded in 2007 in Malmö, Sweden, as Neo Technology by Emil Eifrem, Johan Svensson and Peter Neubauer; later headquartered in San Mateo, California, and renamed Neo4j, Inc.
openness_notes: Community Edition was GPLv3 and Enterprise Edition AGPLv3 (with commercial licences on the side), so the whole product was OSI-licensed (dual licensing, 3). In 2018 Neo4j added the Commons Clause to the Enterprise AGPL and then stopped publishing Enterprise source, making Enterprise proprietary; Community stays GPLv3. Level 2.

license_history.license: Enterprise: AGPLv3 + Commons Clause, then proprietary

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Neo4j sued over the fork's removal of the Commons Clause and prevailed in US federal court; ONgDB development stopped (unverified)

risk_events: 2018: Enterprise Edition closed; litigation against the ONgDB fork's backers (unverified)
robustness: Single-vendor control of Enterprise; Community Edition stays GPLv3. The query language was opened as openCypher and fed into the ISO GQL standard, which spreads the standard beyond the vendor.
openness_effect_assessment: Not assessed: no sourced research was possible in this session.
key_takeaway: Draft only. Neo4j fought a fork of its relicensed code in court rather than in the market and won, the opposite of OpenSearch or Valkey, where hyperscaler backers made forks durable. Funding, valuation and revenue need sourcing.
